{"notes": "Visit 3 (4:00). The fish is now closed. The tail loop on the right is fully dark and connected to the start, so the gap from visit 2 is gone. Around (28.8, 9-11.5) the pieces are packed tightly and look slightly bunched, probably where the two lines met. I don't know who placed which pieces, so I'm not crediting building from the picture. Collect who-placed-what accounts at the review.

Priya: Spoke up three times this visit, after being silent earlier. She said she had taken the bottom line round the lower tail, proposed a halfway handoff, and at 3:45 said she was just under Leo's end and would join up, asking him to hold. The closed tail matches her account, but it's self-reported and I didn't see her place pieces. Clear communication and good follow-through. Confirm her work with her.

Leo: Coordinated well. He accepted Priya's plan, split the lower curve between them, asked for a shout when close to avoid double-laying, and asked Maya to check the joint. He owns the tail and kept the handoff orderly. Possible overlap at the meeting point; ask him.

Maya: Leo asked her to check the joint. I didn't see her do it or hear her this visit. Her visit 2 collaborative leadership still stands, but I have no direct evidence of her contribution now. Ask her what she checked or placed.

Tom: Silent for a second visit, with no evidence either way. Ask him directly what he built or helped with, and what the 'Thanks Tom' was about.

Next: judge how the fish stands up when pushed, and ask each person what they did."}
